source.translation: R. H. Charles, The Book of Enoch (SPCK, London, 1917; Translations of Early Documents), with introduction by W. O. E. Oesterley
source.retrieved_via: https://web.archive.org/web/2023id_/https://sacred-texts.com/bib/boe/boe.txt.gz (sacred-texts.com blocked automated fetch with a Cloudflare challenge)

people.name: Enoch
people.description: Seventh from Adam, son of Jared; the seer and scribe of righteousness who receives the visions and instructs Methuselah.
people.identity_note: Speaks in the first person through most of the book; refs are limited to verses naming him or identifying him unambiguously (e.g. addressing "my son Methuselah", "my grandfather" in Noah's speech). 37:1 gives his descent Enoch-Jared-Mahalalel-Cainan-Enos-Seth-Adam; 60:8 and 93:3 call him the seventh from Adam / born the seventh in the first week. 70:1-2 his final translation.

people.name: Edna
people.description: Wife of Enoch and mother of Methuselah.
people.identity_note: 85:3 "Before I took thy mother Edna" (Enoch to Methuselah); 83:2 "before I took thy mother". Same person as Ednî daughter of Dânêl in Jubilees 4:20; the new_id matches the one used in JUB.json.

people.name: Methuselah
people.description: Son of Enoch and Edna, to whom Enoch entrusts his books; father of Lamech.
people.identity_note: 91:1-2 mentions his (unnamed) brothers, the sons of Edna.

people.name: Lamech
people.description: Son of Methuselah; father of Noah, who feared his newborn son was of angelic origin.

people.name: Wife of Lamech
people.description: Wife whom Methuselah took for Lamech; mother of Noah.
people.identity_note: Unnamed in 1 Enoch; Jubilees 4:28 names Lamech's wife Bêtênôs - the new_id "betenos" matches JUB.json.

people.name: Noah
people.description: Son of Lamech, born with radiant appearance; warned of the deluge and preserved with his three sons.
people.identity_note: Chs. 60 and 65-68 belong to the "Book of Noah" fragments in which Noah speaks in the first person (60:8, 65:5-68:1 "my grandfather Enoch"); Charles regards "Enoch" in 60:1 as an error for Noah. 106:16 his "three children" are unnamed.

people.name: Midwife at Noah's birth
people.description: Midwife in whose hands the newborn Noah arose and spoke.

people.name: Jared
people.description: Father of Enoch, in whose days the Watchers descended on Mount Hermon.

people.name: Mahalalel
people.description: Grandfather of Enoch, in whose house Enoch had his first dream-vision of the deluge.
people.identity_note: 83:3-9: Enoch, before his marriage, sleeps in his grandfather Mahalalel's house; Mahalalel interprets the vision.

people.name: Cainan
people.description: Ancestor of Enoch, son of Enos (pre-flood Kenan).

people.name: Enos
people.description: Son of Seth, ancestor of Enoch.

people.name: Seth
people.description: Son of Adam, ancestor of Enoch.

people.name: Adam
people.description: The first man whom the Lord of Spirits created.
people.identity_note: 32:6 Raphael tells Enoch that "thy father old (in years) and thy aged mother" ate of the tree of wisdom and were driven from the garden - Adam and Eve as Enoch's first ancestors. In the Animal Apocalypse (85:3ff.) Adam appears symbolically as the white bull; such symbolic refs are not counted.

people.name: Eve
people.description: The first woman, whom the Watcher Gadreel led astray.
people.identity_note: Named only at 69:6. 32:6 "thy aged mother" (see Adam).

people.name: Abel
people.description: Slain by his brother Cain; his spirit in Sheol pleads against Cain's seed.

dated_events.event: Vision of the quaking of the heaven of heavens: "In the year five hundred, in the seventh month, on the fourteenth day of the month in the life of +Enoch+"
dated_events.note: Year of a person's life, not a jubilee date. Charles marks "Enoch" as corrupt (+...+); this section belongs to the Book of Noah and the year 500 fits Noah (cf. Gen 5:32). Not convertible to A.M. without assuming Noah's birth year.

dated_events.event: Enoch: "I was born the seventh in the first week" (Apocalypse of Weeks)
dated_events.note: "Week" here is one of the ten world-weeks of the Apocalypse of Weeks (93:3-10, 91:12-17), not a seven-year week of years; "seventh" is his generation from Adam.

excluded_names.Danel: Watcher (6:7) - not the Danel father of Edni in Jubilees
excluded_names.Baraqijal: Watcher (6:7, 8:3) - not the human Barakiel of Jubilees
excluded_names.Son of Man / Elect One / Anointed / Mess: heavenly messianic figure, not entered as a historical person (71:14 is read by some as identifying him with Enoch)
excluded_names.Animal Apocalypse figures (chs. 85-90): Adam, Eve, Cain, Abel, Seth, Noah and his sons, the patriarchs, Moses, etc. appear only as symbolic animals (bulls, sheep, rams) and are not named; not counted as refs

notes: Source: R. H. Charles, The Book of Enoch (SPCK, 1917; Translations of Early Documents), sacred-texts.com /bib/boe/. sacred-texts.com returned a Cloudflare challenge to curl, so the site's own plain-text edition (boe.txt.gz) was fetched from the Internet Archive's capture of https://sacred-texts.com/bib/boe/boe.txt.gz and saved under dl/charles/boe/ (the chapter HTML pages were only partly retrievable because of rate limiting). Chapter:verse follows Charles's numbering as printed; Charles transposes text (91:12-17 is printed after ch. 93; ch. 92 precedes 91:1-11), and the refs use the printed chapter/verse labels. Editorial section headings were stripped before parsing. A few verse numbers are absent from the scan and those verses are merged into the previous one (e.g. 10:7, 10:14, 10:16, 14:10, 16:3, 18:6, 22:4, 60:5, 60:16, 76:13, 82:14, 91:14, 93:2, 100:2, 106:17). 5:5-9 contains Charles's sub-lettered verses (6a, 7c...) merged into 5:5. Only humans are entered. All Watchers, archangels and other angelic/demonic names are excluded; the Animal Apocalypse (85-90) is symbolic and its figures are not counted. Cross-book ids: Edna (85:3) uses new_id edni-enoch-wife and Lamech's unnamed wife (106:1) uses new_id betenos, matching JUB.json, where Jubilees names them (Ednî 4:20; Bêtênôs 4:28). 1 Enoch gives no jubilee/week/year dates for people; the only numeric dating is 60:1 (year 500 of a patriarch's life, text corrupt) and the world-week of Enoch's birth (93:3). No explicit ages are stated.
